comments.note: The existing CanUpdateReference() used _mainViewModel.CreateReferenceCommand (no null guard). Since _mainViewModel is now null in the test constructor, I updated it to _mainViewModel?.CreateReferenceCommand. This is a safe improvement that doesn't change production behavior (MainViewModel is never null in production) but makes the method null-safe.

UpdateDiffState() now contains a long sequence of OnPropertyChanged calls. As the VM grows, this list will become unwieldy. A future improvement could group all sidebar-related property notifications into a private RefreshSidebarProperties() helper, mirroring how some other VMs batch related notifications.

The count text properties (RemovedModCountText, etc.) call DiffLines.Count(l => l.ChangeType == X) each time they are accessed. This duplicates the LINQ query already run by the corresponding count properties (RemovedModCount, etc.). Since the properties are called from UpdateDiffState() in a batch, this is not a performance concern, but a future consolidation could eliminate the duplication by having the count text properties call the count properties directly (e.g., RemovedModCount == 1 ? ... : string.Format(..., RemovedModCount)) — which is already the implemented pattern. No action needed.

summary: Reviewed DiffDialogViewModel.cs (lines 1–685) and DiffDialogViewModelTests.cs (357 lines) in full.
All 7 acceptance criteria are architecturally sound and correctly implemented.

One Blocking issue identified: Dispose() dereferences _mainViewModel without a null guard, but the test-only constructor sets _mainViewModel = null!. Any caller that wraps a test instance in a using-block — or any future test that calls Dispose() — will receive a NullReferenceException. The test seam was introduced without hardening the full IDisposable lifecycle contract.

One minor asymmetry noted (Fix-Forward eligible): ShowReplacementGuidance inlines ReplacedModCount > 0 directly, while the analogous Show* properties all use named HasXxxMods intermediates. Not blocking, but recorded for Developer awareness.
Test file is well-structured with clear Arrange-Act-Assert, proper singular/plural boundary coverage, dynamic PropertyChanged event capture, and correctly documented skipped tests.

comments.note: BLOCKING — Dispose() is unsafe when _mainViewModel is null. The test constructor on line 96–111 assigns _mainViewModel = null! (line 98), yet Dispose() on lines 675–683 dereferences _mainViewModel three times without a null check (_mainViewModel.PropertyChanged, _mainViewModel.GetFileMonitoringCoordinator(), _mainViewModel.GetConfigurationCoordinator()). Any caller that wraps a test-constructor DiffDialogViewModel instance in a using-block, or any future test that calls Dispose(), will throw NullReferenceException. Fix: add a null guard at the top of Dispose(): if (_mainViewModel is null) { DiffLines.CollectionChanged -= OnDiffCollectionChanged; return; }. The CollectionChanged handler is wired in both constructors and must always be unsubscribed.

Minor asymmetry in Show*Guidance pattern: ShowRemovalGuidance delegates through the named HasRemovedMods property (line 186), ShowInsertionGuidance uses the pre-existing HasInsertedMods (line 187), ShowAddedGuidance uses the pre-existing HasAddedMods (line 189) — but ShowReplacementGuidance (line 188) inlines ReplacedModCount > 0 directly rather than going through a named HasReplacedMods property. This is not a bug, but breaks the symmetry established by the other three. Consider adding public bool HasReplacedMods => ReplacedModCount > 0; and updating ShowReplacementGuidance to use it. Not blocking — fix at Developer's discretion.

Pre-existing (out of WP-004 scope): UpdateReferenceWithConfirmationAsync() builds separate removedMods/insertedMods lists via Where() rather than using the new HasRemovedMods/HasInsertedMods properties. A future cleanup could unify these. Not a concern for this WP.

[documentation-forward] The growing OnPropertyChanged call list in UpdateDiffState() and the deferred test seam debt (2 skipped ConfirmationMessage tests requiring MainViewModel) should be captured in a tech-debt or known-limitations section of the developer/architecture notes, so future contributors can find and address them.

summary: Reviewed DiffDialogViewModel.cs (lines 1–693) and DiffDialogViewModelTests.cs (392 lines) in full for the rework submission.

Dispose() null guard (lines 677–683): Fix is architecturally correct. `if (_mainViewModel is null)` guard uses the idiomatic C# null pattern. The early-return branch correctly unsubscribes DiffLines.CollectionChanged before returning — no event leak on the test-constructor path. Normal path proceeds with all three coordinator unsubscriptions unchanged. The two-branch structure (unsubscribe in both branches) is slightly redundant but is actually clearer than a shared pre-guard unsubscribe — each path shows its full cleanup responsibility explicitly.

HasReplacedMods symmetry (lines 185–190): Property set is now fully symmetric across all four change types. HasRemovedMods, HasReplacedMods (new), HasInsertedMods (pre-existing), HasAddedMods (pre-existing) all follow the same `=> XxxModCount > 0` expression-body pattern. ShowReplacementGuidance now delegates through HasReplacedMods rather than inlining ReplacedModCount > 0 directly. OnPropertyChanged(nameof(HasReplacedMods)) correctly added to UpdateDiffState().

UpdateDiffState() notification ordering: Logically sound — HasDifferences is set first via SetProperty, followed by legacy properties, then new counts, then HasXxxMods booleans, then Show* visibility properties, then count text strings. WPF binding evaluation is lazy, so ordering within a synchronous batch is cosmetic, but the chosen order correctly mirrors the dependency chain.

Test constructor: `_mainViewModel = null!` with `[EditorBrowsable(Never)]` and `internal` visibility is the correct pattern for VM test seams. Stub commands using `() => Task.CompletedTask` are appropriate.

Test quality: All 26 DiffDialogViewModel tests pass (2 properly skipped with documented rationale). GuidanceVisibility_UpdatesAfterDiffRefresh exercises the reactive chain end-to-end via INotifyPropertyChanged capture. Dispose_WithTestConstructor_DoesNotThrow uses Record.Exception() — correct xUnit idiom. Singular/plural boundary tested at exactly count==1. Naming convention is consistent.
No new blocking or fix-forward issues found. All prior review findings (blocking: Dispose null guard; non-blocking: HasReplacedMods symmetry) are correctly and completely resolved.
